From the diagram, we see that $f(x)$ has roots ${x}_{1}=-1,$ ${x}_{2}=4,$ and ${x}_{3,4}=\pm 2\text{i}.$ Additionally, we're given that the coefficient of the quartic term is $a=1.$ Therefore, we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =a(x-{x}_{1})(x-{x}_{2})(x-{x}_{3})(x-{x}_{4}) \\  & =1(x-(-1))(x-4)(x-(-2\text{i}))(x-(2\text{i})) \\  & =1(x+1)(x-4)(x+2\text{i})(x-2\text{i})\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(x+1)(x-4)(x+2\text{i})(x-2\text{i}) & = \\ ({x}^{2}+x-4x-4)({x}^{2}+(2\text{i}-2\text{i})x-(2\text{i})^{2}) & = \\ ({x}^{2}-3x-4)({x}^{2}+4) & = \\ {x}^{4}+4{x}^{2}-3{x}^{3}-12x-4{x}^{2}-16 & = \\ {x}^{4}-3{x}^{3}-12x-16 & .\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $f(x)={x}^{4}-3{x}^{3}-12x-16.$
